destination.name: Mannum
destination.tagline: Murray River town where the paddle steamers began, with riverside pubs and a dock museum
destination.description: Mannum sits on the Murray River just over an hour from Adelaide. It is known as the birthplace of the Murray paddle steamers, and the dock museum and Mary Ann Reserve tell that story. Riverbank pubs overlook the water, and kayakers head downstream to a bird sanctuary lined with river red gums. Mannum Waterfalls and the Palmer granite outcrops sit a short drive inland.
whyVisit: Cruise the Murray by paddle steamer

goodToKnow.title: Falls flow seasonally
goodToKnow.detail: Mannum Waterfalls flow seasonally, so expect only a trickle in the drier months.

goodToKnow.title: Lenger Reserve timing
goodToKnow.detail: Lenger Reserve is signposted from Punthari and allows no camping. Visit outside the hottest summer months.

destination.bestTimeBlurb: Mild weather in {months} suits river cruises and walks along the Murray.

destination.name: Coorong National Park
destination.coordinates_source: pending serial pin pass (drafted centroid; replace with a visitor point such as Parnka Point or the Meningie area)
destination.tagline: Lagoons, dunes and pelicans in a wetland of international importance
destination.description: Coorong National Park runs along a chain of salty lagoons behind the Younghusband Peninsula, about 200 km south-east of Adelaide. The wetland is of international importance and is known for pelicans and migratory waders. Visitors bird-watch, walk, fish, kayak, camp and drive 4WD tracks, and Ngarrindjeri and European history runs through the park. Access is via Meningie or Kingston off the Princes Highway.
whyVisit: Paddle the quiet lagoon by kayak

goodToKnow.title: Ocean Beach is 4WD only
goodToKnow.detail: Beach conditions change with erosion and dune collapses. Check the park alert and drive only with sand-driving experience.

goodToKnow.title: Fire closures
goodToKnow.detail: The park closes on days of Catastrophic Fire Danger and may close on Extreme days. Check the CFS before you set out.

goodToKnow.title: Pay before you enter
goodToKnow.detail: Campsite fees must be paid before entry and sites are not powered. 42 Mile Crossing is 4WD-only and reachable from the mainland only in summer.
